prompt: What does an LLM observability platform know that a general tracing backend does not?

choices.text: How long each span took
choices.why: Every tracing backend knows that.

choices.text: Which spans belong to which trace
choices.why: That is the definition of a trace, known to all of them.

choices.text: What a model call is
choices.why: Right: its prompt, reply, tokens and price, and around it users, sessions, scores, datasets and prompts.

choices.text: Whether a span ended in error
choices.why: Status is part of every span.

prompt: A search span with no input is unreadable in tree.py. What happens to it in Langfuse?

choices.text: Langfuse fills in the input from the prompt
choices.why: It shows what it was given; nothing more.

choices.text: Langfuse refuses spans without an input attribute
choices.why: It accepted every span the assistant sent.

choices.text: It is merged into the generation that follows it
choices.why: Observations stay separate.

choices.text: It is just as unreadable, on a nicer screen
choices.why: Right. Deciding what to record is the application's work.

prompt: Match each Langfuse container to what it holds or does.

pairs.right: the queue between web and worker

prompt: A query to Langfuse's API right after a replay comes back with fewer traces than were sent. Why?

choices.text: The worker files spans later
choices.why: Right: they are queued, then filed, then visible. Sent now is not in the API now.

choices.text: Because Langfuse limits each project to one request every twenty seconds
choices.why: There is no such limit; the API answered at once.

choices.text: Because the replay keeps running in the background
choices.why: replay.py finishes before the prompt returns.

choices.text: Because ClickHouse restarts after every batch
choices.why: It stays up throughout.

prompt: A small team with no one to run databases must keep customer text inside the company. What follows from this lesson?

choices.text: Use a hosted service, since running six containers is too much
choices.why: Data comes first: hosted means the text leaves.

choices.text: Self-host, and accept that running it is now somebody's job
choices.why: Right. The data question settles it; the operating work has to be found.

choices.text: Stop tracing
choices.why: That throws away everything lessons 1 to 5 built.

choices.text: Send only the token counts to a hosted service and keep nothing else
choices.why: Then the text needed for debugging is kept nowhere.

prompt: What did the assistant need to start sending its spans to Langfuse?

choices.text: The Langfuse SDK in every function
choices.why: No code changed.

choices.text: A rewrite of its spans in Langfuse's format
choices.why: Langfuse reads OpenTelemetry directly.

choices.text: Two environment variables
choices.why: Right: the OTLP endpoint and its header. telemetry.py adds the exporter when the endpoint is set.

choices.text: A new exporter written for the course
choices.why: It is the SDK's own OTLP exporter.

prompt: Why did Langfuse classify the root span ask as a GENERATION?

choices.text: Because it was the longest span
choices.why: Duration plays no part in the classification.

choices.text: Because it is the root
choices.why: Roots are spans unless something says otherwise.

choices.text: Because Langfuse treats every trace as one generation
choices.why: It listed embed and search as other types.

choices.text: Because it carries gen_ai.request.model
choices.why: Right. A span with a model on it looks like a model call to a tool reading the convention literally.

prompt: Langfuse found the session but not the user. Why?

choices.text: The pseudonym was encrypted
choices.why: It was a plain value; the name was the problem.

choices.text: session.id is a name it reads; user.hash is not
choices.why: Right. Unknown names are kept as metadata and used for nothing.

choices.text: The replay had no users
choices.why: Every request carries a user.

choices.text: Users need a Langfuse account each
choices.why: A trace's user is just a value.

prompt: Langfuse shows times in UTC. A trace at 04:46 on its screen happened at what hour in São Paulo? Give the hour, 0 to 23.
Why are Langfuse's names added by a processor at the edge rather than written by assistant.py?

choices.text: They are one tool's names
choices.why: Right: noise anywhere else. A small adapter keeps the choice of tool reversible.

choices.text: Because assistant.py cannot set attributes after it has started
choices.why: It sets app.reply at the end of every request.

choices.text: Because processors run faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: Because Langfuse forbids them in application code
choices.why: It documents them for exactly that use.

prompt: Why could the processor copy the question into langfuse.trace.input but not the reply into the output?

choices.text: The reply is too long for an attribute
choices.why: It already sits in app.reply.

choices.text: The reply comes at the end
choices.why: Right. on_start sees what the span was created with, and at the end the span is read-only in the Python SDK.

choices.text: Langfuse ignores outputs from OpenTelemetry
choices.why: It reads langfuse.trace.output when present.

choices.text: The reply is redacted
choices.why: Redaction changes text; it does not prevent copying.

prompt: Saturday's traces still cost 0 after the prices were added. Why?

choices.text: Saturday's traces had no generations
choices.why: Most of them called the model.

choices.text: The Saturday price was zero in prices.json
choices.why: It was 1.50 and 6.00.

choices.text: Weekend traffic is free
choices.why: No such rule exists anywhere in the course.

choices.text: Langfuse prices a generation when it is received
choices.why: Right. Adding a price later does not reprice what is stored.

prompt: Langfuse's total for Friday was 0.015895 and costs.py's 0.01590828. What was most of the difference?

choices.text: The embeddings, which Langfuse had no price for
choices.why: Right. The difference names what one of the two was missing.

choices.text: Rounding in Langfuse's floating point
choices.why: Rounding to six places explains half a millionth at most; the rest is 639 embedding tokens.

choices.text: Saturday's traces leaking into Friday
choices.why: Saturday's cost 0 in Langfuse and were not in spans.jsonl.

choices.text: The price cut not being applied
choices.why: Both systems applied the price of 30 September.

prompt: Why could the thumbs be sent as scores with a simple loop?

choices.text: Langfuse matches them to traces by time
choices.why: It matches by the trace id it is given.

choices.text: The scores were attached to the sessions only
choices.why: They were attached to traces.

choices.text: They already had the trace id
choices.why: Right, and OpenTelemetry's trace id is Langfuse's. Joined by id from the start.

choices.text: Thumbs are a built-in Langfuse feature that needs no ids
choices.why: Every score names what it is about.

prompt: A value attached to a trace in Langfuse, such as a thumb or a judge's verdict, is called a ___.
Why was LangSmith's SDK pointed at a recorder rather than at LangSmith?

choices.text: The SDK cannot talk to LangSmith from Python
choices.why: It is a Python SDK made for that.

choices.text: The service is hosted
choices.why: Right, and self-hosting is for enterprise customers. What the recorder keeps is exactly what would have left.

choices.text: The recorder is faster
choices.why: Speed was never the reason.

choices.text: LangSmith only accepts LangChain programs
choices.why: @traceable works on any function.

prompt: What did the LangSmith SDK send without redaction? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: The customer's e-mail address, in the inputs
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The model's whole reply
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The environment variables that configured it
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The OpenAI API key
choices.why: Nothing in the recorded bodies carried it.

prompt: In LangSmith's terms, what are a post and a patch of the same run?

choices.text: Two retries of one request
choices.why: Nothing failed; both are part of every run.

choices.text: Two different runs that share an id by accident
choices.why: Same id, same run, on purpose.

choices.text: The run's start with inputs, and its end with outputs
choices.why: Right. A run is sent twice.

choices.text: An upload and its compressed copy
choices.why: Compression was turned off.

prompt: With hide_inputs set to redact(str(v)), what went wrong with the model run's messages?

choices.text: The address was still there
choices.why: It was replaced by [email].

choices.text: The run was not sent at all
choices.why: sent.py printed it.

choices.text: The model's reply was redacted too
choices.why: hide_outputs ran, and found nothing in the reply that its patterns know.

choices.text: The list of messages became the text of a list
choices.why: Right. A careful hook redacts inside the structure.

prompt: After the --redact run, which detail about Joana still left the machine, in her question and in the reply?

choices.text: Her e-mail address
choices.why: redact() replaced it with [email] before anything was sent.

choices.text: Her full name
choices.why: Right. A name has no shape for a pattern to find, and the model, given it, greeted her by it.

choices.text: Her phone
choices.why: Her message carried no telephone number.

choices.text: Her order
choices.why: Her message named no order.

prompt: Which question does this lesson put first when choosing between the two platforms?

choices.text: Where the data is allowed to go
choices.why: Right. Every trace carries what customers typed.

choices.text: Which has more features
choices.why: Features come last.

choices.text: Which one the team has used before
choices.why: Familiarity is not on the list.

choices.text: Which is cheaper per trace
choices.why: Price matters after data and operation.

prompt: What made the choice of tool reversible in this lesson?

choices.text: Langfuse's export feature
choices.why: Export helps leave a tool; it does not keep the code free of it.

choices.text: Running both tools at once
choices.why: Running both doubles the work and decides nothing.

choices.text: Using LangChain everywhere
choices.why: The assistant does not use LangChain at all.

choices.text: OpenTelemetry in the code, and the tool's names in a small adapter
choices.why: Right. The same spans went to a file and to Langfuse.

items: the exporter sends it over OTLP to web
web keeps the batch in object storage and queues a job
the worker files it into ClickHouse

prompt: Match each word to the tool that uses it for the same idea.

pairs.right: a span Langfuse takes for a model call

prompt: A report by day from Langfuse and one from bill.py disagree at every midnight. Which is right?

choices.text: Langfuse, because it computes cost at ingestion
choices.why: When cost is computed has nothing to do with which day it lands on.

choices.text: bill.py, because it uses Decimal
choices.why: Precision is not the difference here.

choices.text: Both of them
choices.why: Right. One counts UTC days and the other São Paulo's: same events, different midnights.

choices.text: Neither: one of them dropped spans
choices.why: The totals agreed to within the embeddings.
